record.paper_title: From P systems to morphogenetic systems: an overview and open problems
record.original_question: Define a notion of descriptional complexity for a morphogenetic system (M system), a computational model in Euclidean space built from floating objects, tiles, protions, and reaction rules, and then construct a computationally universal M system that is minimal with respect to that complexity measure. In doing so, determine whether the smallest universal system can simulate Turing machines with only polynomial slowdown or whether exponential slowdown is unavoidable.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 1 Minimal universal M system: define a descriptional complexity of an M system. Try to construct a minimal M system which is computationally universal, eventually distinguishing polynomial/exponential slowdown compared to the Turing machine.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A morphogenetic system (M system) is a computational model situated in d-dimensional Euclidean space whose configurations consist of: (i) floating objects that move and react in continuous space; (ii) tiles, i.e. rigid d-polytopes that can attach to one another along matching connectors; (iii) protions, which are tile faces capable of selective permeability; and (iv) reaction rules that govern object-object, object-tile, and tile-tile interactions, including creation, destruction, attachment, detachment, and transport. An M system is said to be computationally universal if it can simulate every Turing machine.

(a) Propose a descriptional complexity measure for M systems, taking into account natural ingredients such as the number of distinct object species, the number of tile types, the number of protion types, the number of reaction rules, and possibly the maximum rule arity or the geometric dimension.

(b) With respect to this measure, construct a computationally universal M system that is minimal (in the sense that no M system with strictly smaller complexity, under the chosen measure, is computationally universal), and prove its universality and minimality.

(c) For the minimal universal M system constructed in (b), determine whether it can simulate an arbitrary Turing machine with only polynomial slowdown in the number of computation steps, or whether any such minimal universal M system necessarily incurs exponential slowdown.
artifact.status_search_result: A 2022 Natural Computing article by Sosík and collaborators ("Morphogenetic computing: computability and complexity results") presents two small universal M systems (one self-healing) that simulate Turing machines with only linear slowdown, addressing the existence of small universal M systems and the slowdown question. However, a definitive descriptional-complexity framework together with a proof of minimality has not been established, so the problem appears partially solved rather than fully resolved.

status_evidence.title: Morphogenetic computing: computability and complexity results
status_evidence.snippet: Two small universal M systems (one of them self-healing) are presented; M systems can simulate Turing machines with only a linear slowdown.
status_evidence.claim: Small universal M systems exist with linear (polynomial) slowdown over Turing machines, addressing parts (b) and (c).

status_evidence.title: Morphogenetic systems for resource bounded computation and modeling
status_evidence.snippet: Studies resource-bounded computation in M systems and their relation to P and NP.
status_evidence.claim: Provides complexity-theoretic groundwork for M systems but does not fix a canonical descriptional-complexity measure or establish minimality.
